shared_genus_traits: Succulent herbs with simple fleshy leaves and stems often spreading across the ground.
Flowers generally with two sepals, typically five petals and several stamens.
Many-seeded capsules opening transversely around the circumference (circumscissile), leaving a detachable lid.
look_here_first: START WITH AN INTACT MATURE FRUIT viewed sideways. A narrow but expanded round MEMBRANOUS WING (0.5–1.5 mm) immediately BELOW the transverse opening seam points toward Portulaca umbraticola. On an unwinged capsule compare multiple fresh leaf axils: P. pilosa has LONG conspicuous WHITE HAIR TUFTS and narrow semi-cylindrical leaves; P. oleracea usually has broad flat spoon-shaped leaves and little axillary hair (though tiny hairs can occur). Flower color is secondary. Inspect several fruits/nodes; cultivated hybrids and immature capsules may be misleading.
decision_sequence: Confirm Portulaca by fleshy leaves and a mature capsule opening with a transverse lid; contrast Talinaceae longitudinally splitting fruit.
Examine mature intact capsules side-on with a millimeter scale: a 0.5–1.5 mm encircling wing just below the seam favors P. umbraticola.
If the fruit lacks a wing, inspect fresh axils under 10× magnification: long conspicuous white tufts plus narrow terete-to-hemispheric leaves favor P. pilosa.
Absent or inconspicuous axillary hairs plus broad flat obovate/spatulate leaves favor P. oleracea; check capsule and seed size as support.
If fruit is immature, nodes damaged, or characters conflict, retain Portulaca sp. and revisit with mature capsules and seed close-ups.

species_comparison_matrix.Portulaca umbraticola: expanded membranous encircling wing 0.5–1.5 mm wide

species_comparison_matrix.Portulaca oleracea: flat, obovate/spatulate, apex round to retuse
species_comparison_matrix.Portulaca pilosa: narrow linear to oblong-lanceolate, terete to hemispheric, often acute
species_comparison_matrix.Portulaca umbraticola: flat, obovate/spatulate or sometimes lanceolate, apex round to truncate

species_comparison_matrix.Portulaca pilosa: conspicuous white tufts at nodes and inflorescences

species_comparison_matrix.Portulaca oleracea: black/dark brown; smooth to granular or stellate cells with rounded tubercles
species_comparison_matrix.Portulaca pilosa: black/leaden; loosely arranged stellate or rounded-stellate short-tuberculate cells
species_comparison_matrix.Portulaca umbraticola: gray; stellate cells with relatively long tubercles

overlap_cautions: P. oleracea and P. umbraticola have overlapping flat spatulate leaves; the mature winged capsule is the stronger separator.
Flower diameter, capsule diameter, seed size and involucre counts overlap; do not key species from one measurement.
Axillary hairs can be lost with age or damaged in collected material; inspect multiple fresh nodes.
Other narrow-leaved Portulaca outside this approved three-species pool may resemble P. pilosa; consult the full Flora of North America key for uncertain plants.
Flower color and overall plant habit are not primary diagnostic characters.
An immature or partially opened capsule may conceal or damage the wing. Photograph intact mature fruit first.
Learner admission does not certify native-range status; preserve independent range metadata.

local_source_pool_lookalikes.separating_character: Consult Flora of North America fruiting key, mature seed-coat sculpture, root form and capsule dimensions before assigning P. pilosa.

diagnostic_photo_checklist.shot: Matched side-on mature intact fruits with 1-mm scale; arrows mark membranous wing, seam and lower cup.
Matched 10× macros of several fresh nodes; arrows to axil and conspicuous or inconspicuous hairs.
Same-scale flat versus terete/hemispheric mature leaf macro; annotate section and outline.
Overhead flowering-head macro with individual subtending leaves numbered.
Mature seed with 0.1-mm scale and seed-coat tubercle labels under microscope.
Intact and opened capsule at matched scale, with lid and cup arrows.
Side-by-side transverse-lid versus longitudinal-valve capsule, arrows marking dehiscence lines.

visual_comparison.title: Purslanes — see the seed capsule wing, white axil hairs and true leaf shape

visual_comparison.memory_rule: WING around capsule = UMBRATICOLA • WHITE HAIR at nodes + NARROW leaf = PILOSA • BROAD SPOON leaf + UNWINGED capsule = OLERACEA.

items.label: Common purslane — broad fleshy SPOON-SHAPED leaves
items.image_role: Full flat obovate/spatulate leaf blade in living plant
items.caption: Look at the wide, flat fleshy leaf narrowing toward its base. This is unlike the slim almost cylindrical leaves of P. pilosa. Shape alone may overlap P. umbraticola; look for an intact capsule.
items.creator: Harry Rose
items.source_region: Australia; not Central Texas range evidence
items.annotation_note: Checked 960x720 source preview: arrow points inside actual green broad blade in center-right, not a stem/flower. Image is unmodified; arrows are learner overlays.
items.photo_status: PHYSICAL_IMAGE_PRESENT; original source photo license preserved; any arrow overlay added by learner

items.label: Common purslane — capsule opens with a horizontal LID
items.image_role: Two-stage original source montage, closed-to-open capsule (pyxis) and real black seeds
items.caption: A photographed before/after sequence shows the green pod opening along a transverse horizontal seam to leave a cup of black seeds. The BIG gray arrow is ALREADY in the photographer's original image; no new overlay arrow added here. Scale bar reads 1 cm for the source montage.
items.creator: Didier Descouens / Muséum de Toulouse
items.source_region: Toulouse, France; anatomy only, not Texas provenance
items.annotation_caution: Existing large gray montage arrow is baked into source photo and is NOT a diagnostic part arrow; no extra arrow implied.
items.photo_status: PHYSICAL_IMAGE_PRESENT; original source photo license preserved; any arrow overlay added by learner

items.label: Shaggy purslane — real WHITE HAIR TUFTS between narrow leaves
items.image_role: Real white axillary trichomes and narrowly semicylindrical succulent leaves
items.caption: WHITE wispy strands here are genuine hairs growing from the leaf axils, not fungal webbing. Compare the relatively narrow almost round-in-cross-section fleshy leaves; inspect several fresh nodes since hair density varies.
items.creator: Forest & Kim Starr
items.source_region: Maui, Hawaii; species diagnostic photo, not local provenance
items.annotation_note: Checked 960×720 source preview: white trichome bundle clearly visible around stem node at x38%,y54%; narrow pointed leaf near x37%,y23%. Both point to genuine photographed structures.
items.photo_status: PHYSICAL_IMAGE_PRESENT; original source photo license preserved; any arrow overlay added by learner

items.label: Wingpod purslane — WINGED mature capsule near opening seam
items.image_role: Capsule with a narrow pale circular rim at the opening / lid seam
items.caption: Notice the bright circular membranous WING around the small central green capsule (not the broad leaf edges). Published FNA describes an expanded ring ~0.5–1.5 mm just below the suture. CAUTION: photographer labeled this cultivated 'Wildfire' material at a nursery in Maui; this PHOTO is not evidence for a wild Texas subspecies.
items.creator: Forest & Kim Starr
items.source_region: Kahului Maui nursery cultivated cultivar Wildfire (NOT Texas native voucher)
items.annotation_note: Checked 960×720 preview: narrow whitish annulus at roughly x60–63%,y46–49% borders circular green capsule near central-right foliage. This label describes visible wing/rim; millimeters from FNA, not measured from photo.
items.photo_status: PHYSICAL_IMAGE_PRESENT; original source photo license preserved; any arrow overlay added by learner

items.caption: A second P. pilosa photograph for field familiarity: flower color can vary and does not replace the diagnostic axillary hair tufts. Check leaves and capsules.
